snackbar-v2.content:
Usage



Toast Options



Persistent Toasts

Set duration: Infinity for a toast that never auto-dismisses.



actionButton.autoDismiss is separate from the toast duration. Set it to false when
clicking the action should keep the persistent toast open. The close button remains
available.

A persistent toast is exempt from dismissOnClickAway, so clicking elsewhere on the page
closes ordinary toasts but leaves it open. It is also kept inside the visible-toast
stack, so newer toasts cannot push it out of view.

It is still a toast: it overlays the page, supports a single action, and is announced once
by screen readers. For a message the user must not miss, use AlertV2 (inline, in reading
order, supports a primary and secondary action) or ModalV2 (blocking).

Do not use duration: 0

duration: 0 does not create a persistent toast. 0 is falsy, so it falls through to
the 4000ms default and you get an ordinary 4-second toast. Because 0 is a valid number,
TypeScript cannot catch this, so a console warning is logged in development builds.

Choosing the right component

| Message                                                                               | Component                              |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| Transient and passive — "Saved", "Copied"                                             | SnackbarV2                           |
| Optional action, no deadline — "Upload failed / Retry", "Undo"                        | SnackbarV2 with duration: Infinity |
| The user must act, or ignoring it has a consequence — session expiry, unsaved changes | AlertV2 (inline)                     |
| The user must act before continuing                                                   | ModalV2 (blocking)                   |
| Must survive navigation or be re-findable later                                       | Neither — needs a notification centre  |

Snackbars support a single action and live in a stack, which makes them a poor host for
anything with a deadline or a consequence. Reach for AlertV2 there: it is inline, always
visible, and supports a primary and a secondary action.

Contributing to Blend Design System

We welcome contributions from the community! Whether you're fixing bugs, adding new components, improving documentation, or proposing new features, your contributions help make Blend better for everyone.

Before You Start

Getting Help

- GitHub Discussions: Ask questions and share ideas
- Issues: Report bugs and request features

Development Setup

Prerequisites

- Node.js 18+
- pnpm (recommended package manager)
- Git for version control

Fork and Clone



Install Dependencies



Development Workflow



Project Structure

Understanding the monorepo structure:



Types of Contributions

Bug Fixes

1. Check existing issues before creating new ones
2. Include reproduction steps and expected vs actual behavior
3. Update documentation if needed

Example Bug Fix Process:



Documentation

Documentation improvements are always welcome:

- Improve existing component documentation
- Add usage examples and best practices
- Update getting started guides
- Fix typos and improve clarity

Design Tokens

When proposing design token changes:

1. Create an issue first to discuss the change
2. Ensure backward compatibility where possible
3. Update all affected components
4. Include design rationale and use cases

Documentation Standards

Component Documentation

Each component should include:

- API Reference: Complete prop documentation
- Usage Examples: Common use cases
- Accessibility: ARIA labels, keyboard navigation
- Do's and Don'ts: Best practices and anti-patterns

Code Comments

- Document complex logic and business rules
- Explain design decisions and trade-offs
- Include links to relevant design specifications

Submission Guidelines

Before Submitting

1. Build successfully: pnpm build
2. Update documentation if needed

Pull Request Guidelines

PR Title Format



PR Description Template



Review Process

1. Automated checks must pass
2. Design team review for UI changes
3. Code review by maintainers
4. Documentation review if applicable
5. Final approval and merge

Release Process

Semantic Versioning

We follow Semantic Versioning:

- Patch (1.0.1): Bug fixes
- Minor (1.1.0): New features, backward compatible
- Major (2.0.0): Breaking changes

Release Notes

Contributors are recognized in release notes:

- Bug fixes and improvements
- New features and components
- Breaking changes
- Special thanks to contributors

Troubleshooting

Common Development Issues

Build failures:



TypeScript errors:

- Check component exports in index.ts
- Verify type definitions are complete
- Ensure all imports are properly typed

Getting Unstuck

If you're stuck:

1. Check existing documentation and issues
2. Ask in GitHub Discussions
3. Reach out to maintainers

Resources

Development Tools

- Storybook: Component development and testing
- TypeScript: Type safety and IntelliSense
- ESLint: Code linting

Design Resources

- Figma: Design files and specifications
- Design Tokens: Token definitions and usage

Learning Materials

- React: Component development
- TypeScript: Type system

Thank You

getting-started.content:
Getting Started with Blend Design System

Welcome to Blend Design System! This guide will help you get started with implementing Blend in your project, whether you're a team member or an open source contributor.

What is Blend?

Blend is a comprehensive design system that provides:

- React Components: Production-ready components with TypeScript support
- Design Tokens: Consistent design tokens for colors, typography, spacing, and more
- Customizable Theming: Flexible design tokens and theme system

Installation

Choose your preferred package manager to install Blend:



Basic Setup

1. Wrap Your App with ThemeProvider

Wrap your application with the ThemeProvider to enable theming:



2. Start Using Components

Import and use components in your application:



3. Custom Theme (Optional)

ThemeProvider (source) automatically loads Blend’s FOUNDATION_THEME and generates component tokens if you don’t pass anything. When you want to tailor the look and feel, pick the approach that fits your needs:

Option 1: Extend Blend foundation tokens

Use the exported FOUNDATION_THEME as a baseline and update only the values you need—colors, typography, spacing, and more:



Option 2: Provide a complete theme

Define your own foundation + component tokens (and optionally breakpoints) when you want 100% control over the design language. The SidebarDemo (source) shows this pattern in action.



Use whichever option matches your project’s branding needs—start simple, then opt in to deeper customization as required. For complete examples of custom token sets, check out the theme definitions in our GitHub repo.

> Component-level tokens
>
> Every component ships with its own ComponentNameComponentTokens type (documented on each component page under Component Tokens). To adapt a component:
>
> 1. Open the component doc and review the token table—it shows the exact shape (backgroundColor.primary.default.default, etc.).
> 2. Import the token type so TypeScript guides you while editing.
> 3. Spread the existing token object and override just the keys you need. Values accept any valid CSS string—use foundation tokens for consistency or drop in a custom color/gradient for brand-specific styling.



Any updates you make to component tokens immediately reflect in the UI—ideal for tweaking spacing, typography, states, or colors on a per-component basis while leaving the global foundation tokens untouched.

Design Tokens

Blend includes a comprehensive set of design tokens for consistent styling:



Best Practices

Component Usage

- Always refer to our component documentation for complete API reference
- Follow established patterns for consistent implementation
- Import only what you need - Blend is tree-shakeable

Design Tokens

- Use design tokens instead of hardcoded values
- Maintain consistency with the design system guidelines
- Customize tokens through ThemeProvider for brand-specific styling

Development Environment Setup

For contributors or those wanting to run the project locally:

Prerequisites

- Node.js 18+ and pnpm
- Git for version control

Setup Steps



Next Steps

1. Explore Components: Browse our component library to see all available components
2. Read Documentation: Check individual component documentation for detailed API reference and examples
3. Contributing: Check our contribution guide to contribute to the project

That's it! You're ready to start building with Blend Design System.

blend-mcp-server-documentation.content:
The Blend MCP Server (blend-ui-mcp) connects MCP-compatible AI assistants — Claude, Cursor, Windsurf, Cline, and others — directly to the Blend design system. Instead of the AI guessing prop names or inventing enum values, it calls the server and gets accurate, manifest-backed answers about every component.

What It Does

The server exposes 11 tools that cover the full component development loop:

- Discover what components exist and search by use-case
- Understand props, enum values, and compound component structures
- Generate correct React JSX with proper imports
- Validate props before shipping — catch typos and invalid enums
- Scaffold complete multi-component UI sections
- Access design tokens for colors, spacing, borders, shadows, and typography

Everything is grounded in the manifest.json that ships with the package — a pre-built snapshot of all component types extracted directly from the Blend TypeScript source.

Installation

Claude Desktop

Open ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json (macOS) or %APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json (Windows) and add:



Save the file, restart Claude Desktop, then verify:

> _"List all Blend design system components"_

Claude should call list_blend_components and return the full catalog.

Cursor

Create .cursor/mcp.json in your project root (or open Cursor Settings → MCP → Add new server):



Windsurf

Edit ~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json:



Cline (VS Code)

Open the Cline panel → MCP Servers tab → Edit Config, then add the same blend-design-system entry above.

The 11 Tools

list_blend_components

Lists all available Blend components, optionally filtered by category.

| Param      | Type   | Required | Description                                                            |
| ---------- | ------ | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| category | string | No       | action, input, data-display, feedback, navigation, overlay |



---

search_components

Search by keyword, use-case, or feature description when you don't know the exact component name.

| Param   | Type   | Required | Description                      |
| ------- | ------ | -------- | -------------------------------- |
| query | string | Yes      | Keywords or use-case description |



---

get_blend_component_props

Returns the full prop list for a component: names, types, required flags, defaults, enum references, and LLM guidance.

| Param           | Type   | Required | Description                       |
| --------------- | ------ | -------- | --------------------------------- |
| componentName | string | Yes      | Component name (case-insensitive) |



---

get_component_variants

Returns all enum types and valid members for a component. Always call this before generating code to know exact enum values.



---

get_component_composition

Returns compound component structure, composition patterns, and usage examples. Essential for components like Accordion, Radio, Switch, and Tabs that require specific parent-child relationships.



---

generate_blend_component

Generates ready-to-use React JSX with correct prop syntax and import statements.

| Param            | Type            | Required | Description                                |
| ---------------- | --------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| componentName  | string          | Yes      | Component to generate                      |
| props          | object          | Yes      | Props key-value map                        |
| children       | string \| array | No       | String content or nested child specs       |
| includeImports | boolean         | No       | Include import statement (default: true) |

Input:



Output:



---

scaffold_blend_section

Generates a complete multi-component UI section. Returns production-ready JSX with imports.

| sectionType                      | Description                                         |
| -------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| fintech_kpi_summary_with_chart | KPI stat cards with a chart                         |
| transaction_list_with_controls | DataTable with search, filters, and actions         |
| interactive_modal_with_form    | Modal with TextInputs and Buttons                   |
| settings_form                  | Settings page with Cards, TextInputs, SingleSelects |
| data_table_with_filters        | DataTable with filter bar, search, export           |



---

validate_component_usage

Validates a props object against the manifest. Catches unknown props, suggests corrections for typos (fuzzy match), and flags invalid enum values.

Input:



Output:



---

get_theme_tokens

Returns Blend design token values by category.

| Category     | Description                                  |
| ------------ | -------------------------------------------- |
| colors     | Full color palette and semantic color tokens |
| spacing    | Spacing scale values                         |
| borders    | Border widths and radius values              |
| shadows    | Shadow definitions                           |
| typography | Font families, sizes, and weights            |

Omit category for an overview of all categories.

Returns server status, manifest metadata, component count by category, and full tool inventory. Useful for verifying the server is connected and up-to-date.



How the Manifest Works

The server ships a manifest.json — a pre-built snapshot of all 50+ component props and enums extracted directly from the Blend TypeScript source. At startup the server loads this file and serves all tool responses from it. No live TypeScript compilation happens at runtime.

The manifest is regenerated automatically before every npm publish via prepublishOnly. To regenerate it manually after component changes:



Adding LLM Context via Meta-Overrides

Each component can have a meta-overrides/.json file with hand-authored descriptions and prop guidance that gets merged into the manifest at generation time:



Environment Variables

Only one variable is supported:

| Variable                     | Default                       | Description                                                                                                          |
| ---------------------------- | ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| BLEND_LIBRARY_PACKAGE_NAME | @juspay/blend-design-system | The package name used in generated import statements. Override only if you have forked or renamed the Blend package. |

Keeping Up to Date

npx caches packages by version. When a new blend-ui-mcp version is published, you get it automatically on the next restart. To force the latest immediately:

theme-provider-token-architecture.content:
A comprehensive guide to understanding and using Blend's sophisticated design token system and theme provider architecture.

Introduction & Overview

What are Design Tokens?

Design tokens are the fundamental building blocks of a design system - the "DNA" of your user interface. They store design decisions as data, making them reusable, consistent, and maintainable across your entire application.

Instead of hardcoding values like #2B7FFF or 16px, design tokens provide semantic names like colors.primary[500] or unit[16]. This approach offers:

- Consistency: Same visual properties across all components
- Maintainability: Change once, update everywhere
- Scalability: Easy theming and brand variations
- Developer Experience: IntelliSense support and type safety

Blend's Token Philosophy

Blend uses a two-tier architecture:

1. Foundation Tokens: Primitive values (colors, typography, spacing) that form the base
2. Component Tokens: Semantic tokens that map foundation tokens to specific component use cases

Architecture Overview



Foundation Token System

Foundation tokens are located in packages/blend/lib/tokens/ and organized into six categories:

Color Tokens

Blend uses a numerical scale from 50-950 for each color family:



Scale Usage:

- 50-200: Light tints for backgrounds and subtle accents
- 300-400: Medium tints for disabled states and secondary elements
- 500-600: Primary colors for actions and emphasis
- 700-800: Dark shades for text and strong emphasis
- 900-950: Very dark shades for high contrast

Typography Tokens

Organized by semantic purpose with complete font information:



Spacing, Border, Shadow & Opacity Tokens



Component Token Architecture

Token Naming Convention

Blend follows: $component.[$target].$property.[$variant].[$type].[$state]

- $component (Required): BUTTON, INPUT, MODAL, etc.
- [$target] (Optional): Component parts - default, iconOnly, inline
- $property (Required): CSS property - backgroundColor, color, padding
- [$variant] (Optional): Semantic variants - primary, secondary, danger
- [$state] (Optional): Interactive states - default, hover, active, disabled

Token Structure Example

Here's a simplified example following the naming convention:



Key Points:

- References foundation tokens - Component tokens map to foundation values
- Not all levels always present - padding skips $state since size doesn't change on interaction
- Semantic naming - Use meaningful names that describe purpose, not appearance

Responsive Design

Tokens are organized by breakpoint first:

Conclusion

Blend's theme provider and token architecture provides:

- Scalable Foundation: Robust base that grows with your needs
- Semantic Component Tokens: Predictable and consistent styling
- Type Safety: Full TypeScript support for confident development
- Responsive Design: Built-in adaptive interface support
- Flexible Customization: Theming without sacrificing consistency

why-we-named-it-blend.description: At Juspay, no two products live in the same world. Learn how Blend was built to make every product feel familiar, no matter where users meet Juspay.
why-we-named-it-blend.content:
At Juspay, no two products live in the same world.

Some are built for consumers making quick payments. Some to support merchants running their businesses or power operations behind the scenes.

Different users. Different contexts. Different pressures.

But for the people using them, these aren't separate products. They're all just Juspay.

And that's where we noticed something important.

Learning One Product Should Help You Use Another

A merchant might move from onboarding to dashboards, reconciliation, or support tools within the same day.

Whenever interfaces changed drastically, users paused — not because tasks were complex, but because they had to re-learn how things worked.

Where is the main action? Is this error critical? Can I safely proceed?

We realized empathy wasn't about making everything look identical. It was about respecting what users had already learned.

Once someone understands one Juspay product, the next shouldn't feel new. It should feel familiar. This belief became the foundation of our design system.

Designing for Difference Without Confusion

Juspay products need flexibility. Teams work across different brands, partners, and product contexts.

So instead of enforcing visual sameness, we asked: Can experiences remain consistent even when visuals change?

Blend enables variety without fragmentation.

For users:

- Interfaces feel intuitive across products
- Interactions behave predictably
- Visual differences don't interrupt understanding

Because when users take critical actions, they shouldn't need to interpret design — only act with confidence.

Consistency Beneath the Surface

In Blend, consistency isn't defined by colors or typography. It lives in behavior.

Across products:

- Actions follow familiar hierarchy
- Feedback appears where expected
- Success, warning, and error states behave consistently

Even as branding evolves, the experience doesn't reset. Users recognize how things work, not just how they look — reducing cognitive effort in operational workflows.

From Design to Code

Blend simplifies how design becomes production.

Instead of translating visuals repeatedly, design decisions are defined as tokens shared between design and engineering. Colors, spacing, typography, and elevation exist as the same system in both Figma and code.

This allows teams to:

- Design components once and reuse them across products
- Implement interfaces without reinterpretation
- Update themes or branding without rebuilding components

Design flows directly into development, reducing gaps, inconsistencies, and implementation effort. Blend turns design and code into parts of the same system.

Why the Name Blend Fits

The name reflects how the system works in practice.

It blends into different product identities. It blends flexibility with structural consistency. And it blends design and engineering through a shared token foundation.

Experiences remain familiar for users, while implementation becomes faster for teams.

Blend isn't just about visual harmony — it connects how products are designed, built, and scaled.

Blend isn't a style. It's a promise:

No matter where users meet Juspay, or which team builds the product, they shouldn't have to start over.

v0.0.14.content:
Dynamic Tab Management - Added comprehensive tab management system
    allowing users to add any number of tabs, seamlessly switch between them via
    an intuitive tab switcher, and close opened tabs with improved user
    experience.



    Add Tab Button - Introduced an "Add Tab" floating button that triggers a
    fully customizable layout, giving developers flexibility to implement custom
    tab creation workflows.







    UI Cleanup - Removed unwanted horizontal scrollbar for a significantly
    cleaner and more professional table interface.



    Configurable Settings - Settings button visibility can now be controlled
    via a dedicated prop, allowing for more customized table configurations
    based on use case requirements.



    Checkbox Default State - Checkbox column is now off by default,
    providing a cleaner initial state and requiring explicit opt-in for
    selection functionality.



    Smart Tooltips - Long-text cells now intelligently show tooltips on
    hover, improving content accessibility without cluttering the interface.



    Pagination Layout Fix - Resolved layout issue where "Rows per page" text
    awkwardly appeared across two lines, ensuring consistent single-line
    display.



    Column Manager Enhancement - Fixed column manager dropdown with improved
    scrollability and prevented actionable elements from being cropped,
    enhancing usability.



    Cell Height Optimization - Added min-height to table cells following
    design specifications to reduce visual congestion and improve content
    hierarchy.



    Header Overflow Protection - Added tooltip functionality in table
    headers when text overflows, ensuring all header content remains
    accessible regardless of column width.







    Design System Alignment - Implemented correct padding and spacing by
    default as per design specifications, ensuring consistent visual hierarchy
    across all popover instances.



    React Element Support (d13921a) - Added comprehensive support for
    passing React elements, enabling fully custom popover UIs tailored to
    specific use cases and design requirements.







    Advanced Formatting System - Introduced comprehensive axis formatting
    types for enhanced data visualization: - AxisType.CURRENCY → Transforms
    125000 into "$125K" for financial data - AxisType.PERCENTAGE →
    Converts 87.5 to "87.5%" for ratio displays - AxisType.NUMBER →
    Formats 1250000 as "1.25M" for large numbers - AxisType.DATE_TIME →
    Renders 1693036800 as "Aug 26, 2023" for temporal data



    Smart Date Display Modes - Implemented intelligent date formatting
    options: - dateOnly: true → Clean date-only display without time
    components - smart: true → Dynamic time display that switches to date
    format when day changes - Default mode → Comprehensive full date and time
    information



    API Restructuring - Streamlined axis configuration by removing
    individual props in favor of grouped settings: - xAxisLabel → Migrated to
    xAxis.label for better organization - yAxisLabel → Now accessible via
    yAxis.label - xAxisInterval → Consolidated under xAxis.interval -
    yAxisInterval → Moved to yAxis.interval for consistency



    Enhanced Customization Props - Added powerful new properties for
    advanced chart customization: - customTick → Support for custom SVG tick
    components - tickFormatter → Flexible custom text formatting functions -
    barSize → Precise control over bar width dimensions - xAxis and yAxis
    → Comprehensive grouped axis configuration objects







    Unified Formatting System - Integrated the same powerful formatting
    support as Charts component, including CURRENCY, PERCENTAGE, NUMBER, and
    DATE_TIME formatting for consistent data presentation across components.



    Enhanced Configuration - Introduced 3 essential new props:
    valueFormatter for custom value display, xAxis and yAxis for
    comprehensive axis configuration, providing complete control over stat
    visualization.







    Multi-Tenant Support - Added comprehensive support for switching between
    any number of tenants, providing scalable tenant management for
    enterprise applications.



    Smart Tenant Limits - Introduced single-select fallback mechanism
    that automatically activates when maximum tenant count (from configuration)
    is reached, ensuring optimal performance and user experience.







    Value Truncation - Added intelligent truncation for values in both
    single and multiselect components, preventing UI overflow while maintaining
    readability.



    Code Organization - Refactored selector logic into a dedicated file for
    improved code clarity, maintainability, and easier future enhancements.



    Form Integration Fix - Resolved critical form submission issues with
    input fields, ensuring reliable data capture and form workflow integration.



    Simplified Interface - Removed action button from default state,
    providing a cleaner interface while maintaining optional action button
    support for specific use cases.



    Flexible Sizing - Added essential props: customWidth and
    customMaxWidth for drawer components, enabling precise responsive design
    control.



    Search Enhancement - Added searchPlaceholder support in single select,
    improving user guidance and search experience customization.







    Prop Mapping Accuracy - Corrected prop mappings for updated components,
    ensuring generated code and Figma design snippets remain perfectly
    synchronized across development workflows.



    MCP Server Integration - Updated mapping logic to work seamlessly with
    Blend MCP servers, enhancing design-to-code workflow efficiency and
    accuracy.







    Design Alignment - Adjusted footer spacing to precisely align with
    design specifications, ensuring consistent visual hierarchy across mobile
    web calendar interfaces.



    Actionable Footer - Added comprehensive support for displaying
    customizable actionable buttons at the bottom, enabling flexible
    call-to-action workflows within drawer components.



    Enhanced Input Clearing - Enabled deletion via Backspace key for
    significantly smoother and more intuitive input clearing experience.



    Smart Focus Management - Introduced auto-focus functionality on
    input boxes, streamlining user interaction and improving accessibility.



    Clipboard Integration - Added robust copy-paste functionality,
    allowing users to efficiently input OTP codes from external sources.



    Configurable Length - Added a flexible prop to configure the number of
    OTP input boxes, supporting various OTP code lengths and security
    requirements.



    Direct Tag Management - Added intuitive ability to remove and destruct
    tags directly from the input field, improving tag management user
    experience.



    Positioning Control - Added comprehensive support for controlling
    dropdown rendering position (left or right alignment), ensuring optimal
    display in various layout contexts.







    New Landing Page (a82a839) - Launched a comprehensive landing page
    for the Blend Design System, providing centralized access to documentation,
    components, and resources for the design system community.

    reflect current usage patterns, clarify project purpose, and provide clear
    community contribution guidelines for open-source collaboration.

    juspay/release/update-stable-version-0.0.13 for stable version deployment.

    PR Template Update - Enhanced pull request template (#301) to improve
    code review process and ensure consistent contribution standards.



    Beta Release - chore(release): v0.0.14-beta [BETA] (#296) for
    comprehensive testing before stable release.

Portal Support - Added portal support for more flexible modal rendering,

    better z-index management and positioning control.

    charts, providing meaningful feedback when no data is available to display.

    labels, legends, and chart text elements for better readability and design
    consistency.



    Axis Spacing - Resolved inconsistent spacing between consecutive ticks
    on the x-axis, ensuring uniform visual spacing and improved chart
    readability.



    Legend Consistency - Fixed "+n more" legend inconsistency issues,
    providing reliable legend display for charts with multiple data series.



    Tick Overlap Prevention - Handled overlapping of first x/y axis ticks,
    ensuring all tick labels remain visible and readable regardless of data
    density.



    ChartContainer Component - Introduced reusable ChartContainer wrapper
    with consistent styling including borders, background, and radius for
    unified chart presentation.



    CoreChart Component - Introduced CoreChart for pure rendering with
    external state support for hover and selection interactions, enabling
    advanced chart customization.



    Advanced Date/Time Formatting - Added comprehensive date/time formatting
    system with timezone support (IANA zones like UTC, EST, PST), 12/24-hour
    format via hour12 prop, smart formatting that adapts to time context, and
    support for multiple input formats (POSIX, UTC strings, JS timestamps).







    Empty State Handling - Added empty state handling for stats components,
    providing consistent user feedback when no statistical data is available.







    Scroll Behavior - Removed unwanted scroll for default table behavior,
    providing cleaner table presentation without unnecessary scrollbars.



    Column Filter States - Added active state for column filter items with
    improved visual feedback and better tooltip positioning for enhanced user
    experience.



    Enhanced Search - Added no result found state in single/multiselect
    components within data tables, improving user feedback during search
    operations.



    Column Management - Updated column filter dropdown with active state
    indicators and improved tooltip positions for better usability.



    Search Bar Focus - Fixed manage columns search bar focus issues,
    ensuring proper keyboard navigation and accessibility.



    Dropdown Alignment - Fixed manage columns dropdown alignment that was
    positioned too far right, ensuring proper visual positioning.



    Design Consistency - Updated search input states, fonts, and design
    tokens for consistent visual design across all table search interfaces.



    Tooltip Enhancement - Improved tooltip positioning in column manager for
    better user experience and accessibility.







    Advanced Selection Control - Updated multiselect to support maximum
    items selected limits and always selected items functionality for better
    data validation and user guidance.



    No Results State - Added no result found state for both single and
    multiselect components, providing clear feedback during search operations.



    Design Alignment - Updated single and multiselect components with proper
    padding, spacing, and design alignment for visual consistency.



    Search Enhancement - Added searchPlaceholder support and improved
    input states for better user guidance and interaction feedback.







    State Typography - Updated font size for hover and active states,
    ensuring consistent text hierarchy and improved visual feedback.



    Active State Cleanup - Removed unwanted border and outline for active
    state, providing cleaner visual presentation.



    Visual Hierarchy - Differentiated title and actionable elements for
    better visual hierarchy and improved user experience.



    Tooltip Support - Added comprehensive tooltip support following the same
    construction pattern as select components for consistent behavior.



    New Component - Added complete Card component support as per design
    specifications, expanding the component library with essential layout
    building blocks.







    Component Documentation - Added comprehensive documentation for each
    component under /docs directory, improving developer experience and
    component usage guidance.



    Landing Page Enhancement - Added changelog page support to the landing
    page (blend.juspay.design), providing centralized access to release
    information.



    Release Workflow - Updated release workflow for Blend library with
    improved automation and introduced new staging branch for better release
    management.
